# a11y-loop

> a11y-loop makes AI coding agents decide accessibility while the work is still being planned, write accessible UI by default, then prove what it can prove with a real browser audit across the states it built — and tell you exactly what it could not check.

This file follows the [llms.txt](https://llmstxt.org/) convention: a concise, machine-readable map
of the project for large language models and AI agents.

## About

- Repository: https://github.com/ChanMeng666/a11y-loop
- Current release: 0.4.1 (2026-10-20) on npm, with provenance. The state of every release and
  channel, and what is pending: docs/roadmap.md, section "State as of 2026-10-20"
- Primary stack: Node.js / JavaScript (ESM), Playwright, axe-core
- License: MIT (axe-core dependency is MPL-2.0 — see THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md)
- Two layers: an Agent Skill (`skills/a11y-loop/`, open Agent Skills standard) covering the plan,
  generation and reporting phases, and a CLI (`src/cli.js`: `audit` / `contrast --fix` / `diff` /
  `plan-check` / `doctor` / `install-browser`) for browser-verified checks and the plan gate
- `a11y-loop mcp` serves the same commands as MCP tools over stdio for MCP-only clients
  (`a11y_loop_audit`, `a11y_loop_diff`, `a11y_loop_contrast_fix`, `a11y_loop_plan_check`,
  `a11y_loop_doctor`, `a11y_loop_manual_checklist`). Each result is the report the matching command
  writes with `--json`, with the same coverage statement and manual checklist. Setup:
  https://github.com/ChanMeng666/a11y-loop/blob/main/docs/overview.md#mcp-server
- GitHub Actions: the repository root is a composite action (`action.yml`):
  `uses: ChanMeng666/a11y-loop@<tag>` with `target`, optional `baseline`, `fail-on`
  (`violations` | `new` | `never`) and `pr-comment`. It writes a step summary and an optional sticky
  PR comment, and never a score. Example: `examples/github-action/audit.yml`. Ships in release 0.4.0 and
  later (0.3.2 and earlier do not contain it); listed on the GitHub Marketplace from v0.4.1:
  https://github.com/marketplace/actions/a11y-loop-audit
- `a11y-loop plan-check --file plan.md` is the plan gate for any agent or CI job: exit 1 when a
  plan that changes UI work names no accessibility decisions, 0 otherwise, 2 on a usage error. No
  TTY, no browser, no state
- Plus one *optional*, Claude-Code-only layer (`plugin/`, the plugin root, published by the root
  `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`) that enforces the plan phase at plan approval, and the
  audit loop with a `Stop` hook that declines, once per session, to end a session that changed UI
  files without running `a11y-loop audit` afterwards (ships in release 0.4.0).
  Other clients rely on the skill text plus `a11y-loop audit` in CI. Installing it copies only
  `plugin/` and fetches no packages. Nothing under `skills/` depends on it. Its hooks run only in
  Claude Code: on Cowork and the Claude apps, where the plugin directory also lists it, only the
  skill's rules apply and nothing is verified.
- Shipped, in progress and planned work: docs/roadmap.md. Planned and in-progress items do not
  exist yet; do not describe them as if they did. Items marked "on main" are not in a tagged
  release until the CHANGELOG has a version section for them
- Privacy: nothing is collected or sent anywhere; see PRIVACY.md
  (https://github.com/ChanMeng666/a11y-loop/blob/main/PRIVACY.md)

## What the skill covers

`skills/a11y-loop/SKILL.md` is four sections, in lifecycle order:

- **§0 Plan rules** — applied while scoping and designing, before any code exists: set the
  conformance target, write accessibility as plan items rather than a trailing "accessibility
  pass", name the product decisions that foreclose accessibility while they are still free to
  change (drag-only reordering, hover-only menus, infinite scroll, canvas-rendered data, time
  limits, CAPTCHA, autoplay), fix the color tokens before components exist, decide structure once,
  and plan the verification.
- **§1 Generation rules** — applied while writing UI code: semantic HTML first, ARIA discipline,
  APG keyboard contracts, labels, focus visibility, AA contrast in light and dark, reduced motion,
  24×24 targets.
- **§2 The loop** — mandatory after any UI change: audit the states you built, fix in source,
  re-audit, diff, repeat until it converges. Requires a real browser.
- **§3 Honesty rules** — what may and may not be said about the result. Binding on everything in
  this repository, including its own documentation.

Reference files under `skills/a11y-loop/references/` are loaded on demand, not upfront:
`plan-phase.md`, `wcag22-quick-ref.md`, `apg-patterns.md`, `ai-failure-modes.md`,
`manual-testing.md`.

## Installing it (for an agent acting on a user's behalf)

Every command is non-interactive, idempotent, and needs no TTY. If a user asks for a11y-loop to be
installed, run these yourself rather than handing them back:

```bash
npm i -g a11y-loop
a11y-loop install-browser                     # Chromium for a11y-loop's own Playwright
a11y-loop doctor                              # exit 0 when an audit can run here
# then ONE of:
npx skills add ChanMeng666/a11y-loop -g -y    # portable skill, any client
claude plugin install a11y-loop --marketplace ChanMeng666/a11y-loop   # OR Claude Code plugin, 2.1.292+
```

Verify: `a11y-loop --version`; `test -f ~/.claude/skills/a11y-loop/references/plan-phase.md` (skill
route); `claude plugin list | grep -A2 'a11y-loop@'` (plugin route, expect `Status: ✔ enabled`).
Do not use `npx playwright install chromium` for an installed CLI: it can resolve a different
Playwright and install a browser this copy cannot launch. Set `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH` the same
way for `install-browser` and for every audit, or leave it unset for both.

Upgrading is a different command from installing (`claude plugin install` on an already-installed
plugin does nothing): `npm i -g a11y-loop@latest`, re-run `npx skills add ChanMeng666/a11y-loop -g -y` (or the `cp`) if using the skill, then
`claude plugin marketplace update chanmeng-a11y-loop && claude plugin update
a11y-loop@chanmeng-a11y-loop`. Teardown is `claude plugin disable|enable|uninstall`; only
`uninstall --prune` needs `-y`.

No `git clone` is required. `npx skills add` fetches the skill from GitHub, and it also ships inside the
npm package (`$(npm root -g)/a11y-loop/skills/a11y-loop`), so a manual `cp -r` into `~/.claude/skills/` works too.
On Claude Code older than 2.1.292 the plugin takes two commands: `claude plugin marketplace add
ChanMeng666/a11y-loop`, then `claude plugin install a11y-loop@chanmeng-a11y-loop --scope user`.
Do not `cp` over a skill that `npx skills add` installed: it is a symlink, and the copy fails on it.
On Windows use PowerShell or Git Bash, not cmd.exe. Codex: `codex plugin marketplace add ChanMeng666/a11y-loop`, then
`codex plugin add a11y-loop@chanmeng-a11y-loop`. Install the skill *or* the
plugin, not both: the plugin carries its own copy, and doing both makes the model see `a11y-loop`
and the directory-qualified `a11y-loop:a11y-loop`. Prefer `--scope user`; `--scope project` writes a
committable `.claude/settings.json` but puts the plugin behind Claude Code's workspace-trust prompt
on first open, which is a security boundary and must not be circumvented. A new session is needed
before a newly installed skill or hook takes effect.

- [Distribution briefing](https://github.com/ChanMeng666/a11y-loop/blob/main/docs/research/distribution.md): where the project is listed and on what rules (2026-10)
- [CHANGELOG](https://github.com/ChanMeng666/a11y-loop/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md): version history
- [Docs site](https://ChanMeng666.github.io/a11y-loop/): the same material as a guide

## Coverage, stated honestly

Automated testing reaches a minority of WCAG failures, and this project says so in every report.
Deque puts automation at ~57% of issues by volume of individual instances; only 17 of the 55 WCAG
2.2 A/AA criteria (31%) have any ACT-approved automated rule, and accessible.org counts 7 of 55
(13%) as reliably flagged. Nine A/AA criteria cannot be meaningfully tested by any tool. A clean
audit means "no automatically detectable failures in the states that were driven" — never that
anything is accessible or conformant.

The engine is also wrong in a few known places, and those are documented rather than suppressed.
Read Field Notes (above) before concluding that a `div-button` row on `<body>` or a run of
`keyboard-unreachable` findings is a defect. Forced-colors `color-contrast` rows arrive under
`needsReview` with a `note` and `routedFrom: "violation"`, never as violations, and they are still
reported. Checking a row against its explanation is part of the loop; dropping rules is not, and
a11y-loop drops none.

## Reading a report

JSON reports are `schemaVersion: 2` and only add to version 1. Each finding has `evidence`:
`measured` (a value read off the page against a threshold), `inferred` (concluded from a bounded
keyboard, dialog, route-change or status-message probe, still a blocking violation, with `confidence` when the probe ran out of
budget) or `needs-review`. The top-level `clusters` array groups rows by shared cause (a colour
pair for contrast, a selector pattern otherwise) and gives the fix once; every row also stays in
`findings`. Count failures in rows, not clusters. The terminal output prints the summary and the
clusters first; `--verbose` lists every cluster member.

## For agents

To work effectively here: read docs/overview.md and AGENTS.md first, then follow the commands and
conventions they describe. Prefer the project's own scripts over ad-hoc commands.

Two rules carry more weight than the rest:

1. **Never weaken the honesty language** (§3 of SKILL.md) anywhere — code, docs, tool output, or
   this file.
2. **Keep the skill portable.** Nothing under `skills/` may depend on `plugin/`, and no Claude-Code-specific mechanism may appear in `SKILL.md` or
   `references/`. The same `SKILL.md` is meant to work in any client implementing the Agent Skills
   standard.

If you are being asked to plan or write UI code in a project that has installed the `a11y-loop`
skill, read `skills/a11y-loop/SKILL.md` and treat it as binding, not this file.
